subject: chemistry

hotspots.label: The nucleus
hotspots.description: This dense bundle of spheres at the center is the nucleus — the tiny, heavy core of the atom. Everything else is empty space and orbiting electrons.
hotspots.positionHint: The small bundle of red and gray spheres at the center.
hotspots.function: Marks the atom's dense central core.

hotspots.label: Protons and neutrons
hotspots.description: Inside the nucleus are the protons (red) and neutrons (gray) — the heavy particles that give the atom its mass and identity.
hotspots.positionHint: The red and gray spheres packed inside the nucleus.
hotspots.function: Shows the protons and neutrons packed in the core.

hotspots.label: The positive pull
hotspots.description: The nucleus's positive charge reaches across the empty space and pulls the negative electrons in — holding the whole atom together.
hotspots.positionHint: The glow and arrows from the nucleus toward the cloud, visible when the pull layer is on.
hotspots.function: Shows the nucleus pulling the electrons into orbit.

visualStyleNotes: Chemistry palette, Anatomy Atelier bar: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with a soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no props. An atom cross-section floats centered, lit with soft neutral studio light — no rim-light glow, no bloom, no emissive anywhere. Clean stylized product-render look, specimen-quality not cartoon. Nucleus: small soft red and gray spheres packed tightly; electron cloud: huge translucent warm-white shell; wide empty gap between them. Strong saturated color is reserved for the small flat hotspot dots (coral / amber / molecular-green accents from the Chemistry palette). Slow auto-rotation, calm, minimal chrome.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0 everywhere, single 2K shared texture atlas. Protons: soft muted red, roughness ~0.4. Neutrons: soft muted gray, roughness ~0.4. Cloud shell: translucent warm-white, alpha ~0.1. No emissive channels anywhere — any glow is handled by app runtime UI.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: an atom cross-section focused on the nucleus, built to be read as 'tiny, dense, positive core — the heart of the atom.' Three procedural layers, all clean primitives:

1) MAIN: a small nucleus bundle at center — ~6 soft red proton spheres and ~6 soft gray neutron spheres (radius ~0.22 each) packed together — surrounded by a very large translucent warm-white electron cloud sphere (radius ~1.9, alpha ~0.1) with a clearly visible wide empty gap between nucleus and cloud. One quarter of the cloud cut away so the nucleus is unobstructed.

2) SCALE REVEAL (toggleable layer): the cloud fades to near-invisible and the camera eases closer (app-driven) to the nucleus alone — emphasizing how small and dense the core is. A faint ruler or scale bar appears (app-rendered).

3) PULL (toggleable layer): soft arrows and a glow emanate from the nucleus toward the cloud (app-rendered), showing the positive charge attracting the negative electrons.

Camera: framed so the whole atom fits with the nucleus clearly visible at center; auto-rotate default. Budget 6-10k triangles. Named nodes: NucleusBundle, Protons_06, Neutrons_06, ElectronCloud, CutawayPlane, PullArrows. All labels are hotspot dots in the app layer.
